intro: Timeless had no formal titles. It was run by three people who came at Overwatch from different directions: a voice, an operator and a builder. These are their stories up to November 2026.

people.name: Chase
people.summary: Chase came to Timeless as a working Overwatch social media pro. His résumé includes Dallas Fuel, NRG and zoned. He co-founded Timeless, stayed through every version of it, and today runs social for LuneX and the US World Cup team.

chapters.d: By late 2024 Chase had worked in Overwatch for about five years, on social for teams including Dallas Fuel and NRG.
Co-owner from day one. For the first anniversary he wrote a long thread calling Timeless a passion project.
When the roster moved to NTMR for the EWC, Chase went with it as director. He called fielding a team at an international LAN a dream come true as NTMR headed to the 2024 World Finals in Stockholm.
Returned as a Timeless owner for the 2025 OWCS run with the WISP core.
Social for LuneX Gaming, the US World Cup team and Point of View.

people.name: Jacob "Doc" Scott
people.summary: Doc brought the operations side. He advised NTMR during its EWC and World Finals run, then helped run its expansion into other games. He came back to Timeless as an owner for 2025.

chapters.d: Joined NTMR as an advisor alongside the ex-Timeless roster, through the EWC and the 2024 World Finals.
Named one of NTMR's esports operators for its Valve titles and future games as the org expanded beyond Overwatch.
Listed with Chase as a Timeless owner for the 2025 OWCS season.

people.name: Alex "th3mfg" Scholtes
people.summary: Alex built the group that became Timeless. He started with Hour Zero in 2020, kept going through Kaizen, and co-founded Timeless with Chase in October 2022. Away from Overwatch he is a software engineer.

chapters.d: Alex has worked as a software engineer since 2017, mostly on Ruby on Rails platforms: multi-tenant data models, background job pipelines and the integrations that connect a product to other companies' software. He designed and built Hour Zero's website, the first software he shipped for an operation with real money and real users behind it. He now builds his own tools as well, among them FPS, a set of AI coding agents that each hold one job, which helps maintain this archive.
The first team. Hour Zero won Trial of Champions in October 2020 and played Contenders qualifiers. It doubled as a classroom: several of the people who later ran Timeless came up through it.
The second team, as the group kept growing. aramori, now Sentinels' first female Marvel Rivals pro, came through Hour Zero and Kaizen.

Alex and Chase launched Timeless. Alex's job was building: figuring out what was fixed and what could change, clearing space for people with creative ideas, and backing an individual against the group when he thought they were right.
Contenders, the league's Pro-Am, a Flash Ops title, then 2nd in OWCS NA Stage 1 behind Toronto Defiant, all on a fraction of what the established orgs spent.

After the team beat NRG Shock for an Esports World Cup seed, the owners split over whether to go. Alex voted to go. Most of the co-owners and much of the staff chose not to, and the roster went to Riyadh under NTMR. He says he's still on good terms with everyone from that period.
With Timeless back competing and its alumni across OWCS, Alex is working on bringing in sponsors to build the next version properly.
